part.text:
All tests pass — `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` with every `ZipperTest` case green.

Implementation in `src/main/java/Zipper.java`:

- **`Zipper`** — a mutable focus node holding `value`, `left`, `right`, and an `up` back-pointer to the parent.
  - `toTree()` walks up to the root and wraps it in a `BinaryTree`.
  - `setLeft`/`setRight` install the child and set its `up` pointer, returning `this` for chaining.
  - `equals`/`hashCode` compare `value`, `left`, `right` (deliberately ignoring `up`, since back-pointers shouldn't affect structural equality).
- **`BinaryTree`** — wraps the root zipper; `printTree()` renders the exact expected format (`{ value: ..., left: ..., right: ... }` for children, bare at the root), and `equals` compares root zipper structure so `assertThat(zipper.toTree()).isEqualTo(binaryTree)` works.

Because the zipper shares the tree's nodes in place, operations like `zipper.left.right.up.setValue(5)` and `differentPathToSameZipper` work naturally — both paths land on the same object.
